source.title: Maximum Number of Operations to Move Ones to the End

teaching.hint: When a one moves, does it cross one zero or one entire zero run, and can it ever cross that same run again?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Each one can cross each original zero block to its right exactly once in a complete sequence. A move crosses a whole block, so block width does not affect the operation count.
solution_outline.approach: Scan the original string left to right, counting ones seen. Whenever a zero block begins after a one, add the number of preceding ones to the answer.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: At each position, the ones count equals the number of ones to the left. The accumulated answer counts every pair of an earlier one and a zero block begun so far exactly once.
solution_outline.correctness: A move carries one across a complete zero block and only moves right, so it cannot cross the same block twice. Every one originally left of a block can eventually cross it as operations continue; no move can cross a block to its left. Thus each eligible one/block pair contributes exactly one move, and scanning block starts counts all such pairs.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for a string of length n; the answer can be quadratic in n.
solution_outline.pitfall: Counting every zero separately overcounts moves across a wide zero run; counting only zero blocks undercounts when several ones wait to cross one block.

accepted_alternatives: Scan from right to left, counting zero blocks seen and adding that count for each one; this is also O(n) time and O(1) space.
common_wrong_turns: Count zero characters instead of blocks
Assume each one can move only once
source_fidelity_notes: The source's move trace was replaced by a wide-zero-run example; full-run movement, repeatability, maximum count, and length bound were retained.
